methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $103M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Equilibrium Energy is a Series B climate and energy company that has raised $103M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private peers and 1 public comparable (Linamar, ticker LNZA) across the climate and energy sector, including later-stage entrants such as KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy for current valuation and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yields $196M. The peer-median approach anchors to the median valuation of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), producing a $1.0B implied valuation. This peer cohort exhibits material dispersion, with valuations ranging from $700M to $3.0B.

Synthesis of both methods produces a triangulated range of $166M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $598M. The wide spread reflects uncertainty inherent in stage-progression methods for early-stage companies and meaningful heterogeneity within the peer set itself. Key sensitivities include the stage-transition multiplier assumption and peer selection within the climate-tech segment, where valuation dispersion remains elevated relative to more mature sectors.
